Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! We can see the Afghanistan players in a huddle who now spread out to take their respective field positions. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis are the two openers for Sri Lanka. Rahmanullah Gurbaz will not be keeping and it is the debutant, Mohammad Ishaq who has the gloves. Wafadar Momand to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Sri Lanka's bowling effort was a bit disappointing, especially in the initial stages of the innings where they struggled to contain the Afghan openers, conceding 72 runs in the Powerplay. A missed opportunity with Akila Dananjaya dropping Rahmanullah Gurbaz proved costly for them. However, they managed to stage a comeback in the middle overs, with their spinners, particularly Akila and skipper Wanindu Hasaranga, making crucial breakthroughs. Despite some expensive spells from the pacers, Dasun Shanaka stood out with his economical bowling. Matheesha Pathirana's impressive penultimate over, where he picked up two wickets and came close to a hat-trick, provided a late surge for the hosts. Now, Sri Lanka's batters face a daunting task in their run chase, while Afghanistan will be confident of defending their total and salvaging a victory to end the tour on a high note. Stay tuned for what promises to be an exciting run chase.

A late flurry from the debutant and Afghanistan finish on a high! They made a blazing start to their innings, with both openers, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, and Hazratullah Zazai, attacking the Sri Lankan bowlers from the outset. Gurbaz, in particular, survived an early scare but capitalized on it to score a scintillating half-century, while Zazai also contributed with a quick start before falling short of his fifty. Despite a brief hiccup with the dismissal of Zazai, Afghanistan continued to pile on the runs, with Gurbaz leading the charge with a brilliant 70 off just 43 deliveries. Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi provided valuable support in the middle overs, with Omarzai playing the aggressor's role and Nabi anchoring the innings. They struggled a bit towards the end to score the big shot, but Mohammad Ishaq made sure that they go well past that 200-run mark with some lusty blows in the final over.

FOUR! Ishaq finishes off in style with a four! Not exactly where he intended to hit but he gets a boundary anyways. On a fuller length outside off with some pace-off on it, Mohammad Ishaq, the debutant slices it over deep point for a boundary and it makes 17 runs off the final over. What a pivotal cameo from him on his debut. Afghanistan end their innings on a high at 209.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! The umpires make their way out the middle and so do the fielders of Sri Lanka who spread out in the field. Ibrahim Zadran and Hazratullah Zazai are the two openers for Afghanistan. Angelo Mathews has the new ball and is all in readiness to commence the play. Let's go...

Wanindu Hasaranga, the skipper of Sri Lanka says they would have bowled first anyways. Four changes in the team as the bench strength also needs to be tested. Says that they are playing their natural game and it has generated positive results for them throughout the series. Ends up by saying that they will aim to whitewash the opposition.

Ibrahim Zadran, the skipper of Afghanistan won the Toss and elected to BAT first. He says that they will bat first. Adds that the surface looks good and they will look to put a good total on the board. Tells that they will focus on executing their game plan effectively and if they get it right, they will perform well. Informs that they have made four changes and Ishaq is making his debut.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is at the pitchside. He says that it is very very warm. A nice breeze flows across the ground. He adds the deck looks pretty patchy and dry and hard. There is some grass around the length and says that the bowlers can exploit these conditions. Adds that batters in the first innings will enjoy batting and put pressure on the team batting second.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera (In place of Dhananjaya de Silva), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Kamindu Mendis (In place of Charith Asalanka), Angelo Mathews, Dasun Shanaka, Wanindu Hasaranga (C), Akila Dananjaya (In place of Maheesh Theekshana), Nuwan Thushara (In place of Binura Fernando), Matheesha Pathirana.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Hazratullah Zazai, Ibrahim Zadran (C), Mohammad Ishaq (In place of Gulbadin Naib), Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Karim Janat, Sharafuddin Ashraf (In place of Najibullah Zadran), Noor Ahmad, Fareed Ahmad (In place of Naveen-ul-Haq), Wafadar Momand (In place of Fazalhaq Farooqi).
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the coin flip for the third time and they elected to BAT first.

Afghanistan's performance in this series has been below par, highlighting the significant impact of missing key players like Rashid Khan and Mujeeb Ur Rahman. Their batting lineup has struggled, with only one notable fifty from Ibrahim Zadran. In the bowling department, they showed promise in the first match but faltered in the second. Players like Fazalhaq Farooqi, Naveen-ul-Haq, and Noor Ahmad will need to step up their game. Azmatullah Omarzai has shown potential as an all-rounder and could be a key player for them. The Afghans will be eager to salvage some pride with a win in this final match. On the other hand, the Lankans will aim to maintain their unbeaten streak and secure a clean sweep. Toss and team news coming up shortly.

The opening match indeed provided a thrilling contest, with Sri Lanka clinching victory thanks to a stellar all-round display from their captain Wanindu Hasaranga and impressive bowling from Matheesha Pathirana. In the second encounter, their batters, in fine form, laid the foundation for victory, with Angelo Mathews shining brightly to seal the series. With the series already secured, the Lankans may opt to make a few changes to provide opportunities to other players. Their success so far has been a collective effort, with every member of the team contributing in some way. They'll be aiming to maintain this momentum and secure a clean sweep against Afghanistan.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the third and final T20I between Sri Lanka and Afghanistan. The battleground for this game will be the Rangiri Dambulla International Cricket Stadium. With the hosts holding a commanding 2-0 lead in the series, they'll be eager to seal the whitewash, while the visitors, known for their fighting spirit, will be determined to salvage a win and end the tour on a high note. Stay tuned for an exciting match ahead!
... MATCH DAY ...

As the last leg of this series is on the cusp of a finish, Sri Lanka has asserted dominance by winning the One-off Test, and also clean sweeping the ODI series and now the final match of Afghanistan's tour to Sri Lanka is on the horizon, marking the third and last T20I between the two teams at the same Dambulla venue. With Sri Lanka already having clinched the series by 2-0, they enter the match with a tremendous winning momentum from their dominant performances in the previous encounters. The first T20I witnessed an impressive display of death bowling by Matheesha Pathirana, who badly dismantled the timber thrice, while the second match saw the hosts clinching victory in a more commanding fashion. In the second match, Sri Lanka's batsmen made significant contributions, with Kusal Mendis, Pathum Nissanka, and Sadeera Samarawickrama posting useful scores. Skipper Wanindu Hasaranga's brisk 22 off just 9 deliveries complemented Samarawickrama's solid 51, but it was Angelo Mathews' quickfire 42 off 22 balls that propelled the hosts to a daunting total of 187. Despite Mohammad Nabi's economical bowling performance, other Afghan bowlers struggled in the slog overs, unable to contain Sri Lanka's onslaught. In their chase, Afghanistan faced early setbacks, losing wickets rapidly with only Karim Janat and Mohammad Nabi managing to cross the 20-run mark. Despite their efforts, Afghanistan couldn't stabilize their innings, losing half their side within the Powerplay overs. Ultimately, they were bowled out in the 17th over, succumbing to a hefty 72-run defeat. Sri Lankan bowlers, led by Mathews, continued their dominance, with Mathews himself dismissing key batsmen Hazratullah Zazai and Ibrahim Zadran. His economical spell of 2 wickets for 9 runs in 2 overs was instrumental, supported by Binura Fernando, Matheesha Pathirana, and Wanindu Hasaranga, all claiming two wickets each, while Maheesh Theekshana also chipped in with a wicket.  Sri Lanka's batting unit has been firing on all cylinders, while their bowling attack has proven to be lethal throughout the series. Wanindu Hasaranga's remarkable return from injury has been a highlight, showcasing his immense talent. Matheesha Pathirana has garnered praise from the cricketing world, demonstrating his value to the team's bowling lineup despite his relatively young career. Conversely, Afghanistan's batting struggles have left them searching for answers, as they have failed to meet expectations in this series. In the final game, they will be eager to deliver a strong batting performance and address their previous shortcomings. As the series concludes, Sri Lanka will aim to complete a clean sweep, while Afghanistan will seek to salvage pride in the final match of the tour.
